narr: A warm front slowly lifted north across the region during the 6th causing rain and thunderstorms. A low pressure system and associated cold front slowly pushed back across the area on the 7th and stalled into the 9th with a couple rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms.
ev: Heavy rain flooded areas around Willis Flat Road including a shop.
Roads and parking lots flooded in Elizabeth.
Portions of Highways 10 and 13 between Pitkin and Elizabeth were flooded.
Briar Marsh and Turps Roads were flooded.
A USGS gage indicated Barnes Creek exceeded flood stage by 2 feet.
A USGS GAGE reported Buxton Creek rose into moderate flood.
Numerous roads were flooded in Ville Platte.
Numerous roads were flooded in Opelousas and 3 cars were reported as stalled.
Several roads were flooded and closed in Deville.
Several streets in Jennings were flooded.
The Vermilion River rose 2 feet over flood stage. Several streets also flooded around Lafayette.
A gage indicated Chopique Bayou flooded Pete Seay Road. Other roads in the area also flooded.
A USGS gage indicated Bayou Mallet exceeded flood stage.
Numerous roads were flooded around New Iberia.
Numerous roads flooded and impassable in Erath.

Multiple roads from around Bundick Lake to just outside of Deridder were flooded with many impassable. Bundick Lake rose to half a foot over flood stage and was going over the spillway. A section of Charles Libick Road washed out.
Numerous roads were flooded in Lake Charles, Moss Bluff, Sulphur, and Carlyss. One car was stalled in downtown Lake Charles.
A USGS gage indicated the Vermilion River flooded.
Flooding resulted in numerous streets being impassable from Carencro through Youngsville, and Lafayette. Flood water intruded a few homes.
